Inherent to the ad-hoc ActionPane+Group design the case mandates; no standard pattern fits, Custom is the honest value.

root_cause_hypothesis: The three assertions this case exists to test all PASSED: (1) remove-control found DemoScratchButton three levels down (Design>ActionPane>ButtonGroup>Button) with only controlName passed, no parentControl; (2) the emptied ButtonGroup collapsed to the serializer spelling <Controls />; (3) remove-control on a form EXTENSION targeting the base control HeaderNoteId was REFUSED, not silently succeeded. DEFECT FOUND on the completion path the case (and the remove-control op-spec) prescribes for step 5 -- "hide it with modify-property Visible=No on a control extension". d365fo_file(modify, objectType=form-extension, operation=modify-property) cannot express a control-scoped property override and does not refuse when asked for one. It has no control target parameter, and it unconditionally appends the pair into the FORM-LEVEL <PropertyModifications> collection, never <ControlModifications>. Probe A: params={controlName:"HeaderNoteId", propertyPath:"Visible", propertyValue:"No"} returned a headline SUCCESS and wrote <AxPropertyModification><Name>Visible</Name><Value>No</Value></AxPropertyModification> at FORM level -- i.e. it hides the ENTIRE FORM, not the control. A trailing advisory did say "controlName: IGNORED (not read by operation modify-property)", but the wrong write was still committed to disk rather than refused. Probe B: params={propertyPath:"HeaderNoteId.Visible", propertyValue:"No"} returned SUCCESS with NO warning at all and wrote a form-level property literally named <Name>HeaderNoteId.Visible</Name>, which is not a member of AxFormExtension. The form-extension modify-property path therefore accepts an arbitrary unvalidated property NAME. Contrast: the same operation on objectType=table goes through IMetaTableProvider.Update and placed real properties (ReplacementKey, DeveloperDocumentation) correctly, so the gap is specific to the form-extension writer. Net effect: step 5 of this case cannot be completed on the current tool surface without hand-written XML, which the case forbids. The op-spec note for remove-control documents a remedy the toolset does not implement. SECONDARY (lower severity): get_object_info(objectType=form, options={include:"xml"}) served a STALE cached response. After six successful add-control writes grew the file from 866 to 2381 bytes, a second call returned the pre-write 866-byte XML plus a "Duplicate call ... the result above is identical" notice. The dedup cache is keyed on call shape and is not invalidated by intervening d365fo_file writes to the same object, so it can hand an agent a stale view of an object it just modified.
suggested_fix_area: src/tools/modify (form-extension modify-property writer): 1) add a control target parameter (controlName) and route control-scoped properties into <ControlModifications>/AxFormControlModification instead of form-level <PropertyModifications>; 2) until that exists, REFUSE rather than write when controlName is supplied or when propertyPath contains a dot, instead of committing a form-level modification and merely warning; 3) validate the property NAME against the AxFormExtension/AxFormControl metadata surface so an invented name like "HeaderNoteId.Visible" is rejected. get_knowledge op-spec for modify-property: document the form-extension and form-control cases (currently only table/table-extension/edt/class/form-Caption/Pattern are listed), and keep the remove-control op-spec note in sync so it stops pointing at an unimplemented remedy. get_object_info XML dedup cache: invalidate the per-call cache when d365fo_file writes to the same object in the session, or exclude options.include="xml" from dedup entirely. get_knowledge op-spec for add-control: controlType enum omits ActionPane and ButtonGroup, both of which the writer accepts and emits correctly (AxFormActionPaneControl / AxFormButtonGroupControl). Also controlLabel is silently dropped on a Button (correctly warned) -- document Text as the button caption property.
